name: hyprland-monitors
description: The monitor surface: what the compositor answers for `hyprctl -j monitors`, and what the `hl.monitor` configuration call accepts. The Display page reads the first and writes the second, and this record is why it can do both without guessing a field name. Nothing here is inferred from a wiki page or from memory: both halves were read out of the pinned release's source, line by line.
source: Hyprland v0.57.2: src/ipc/s1/Commands.cpp (CCommandFormatter::getMonitorData at :212-330 with its JSON key list at :224-275 and its text format at :326-330, availableModesForOutput at :112-125, SOLITARY_REASONS_JSON at :127-131, monitorsRequest at :378-407, the `monitors` registration at :2112), src/config/lua/bindings/LuaBindingsConfigRules.cpp (the MONITOR_FIELDS table at :81-178, hlMonitor at :1077-1139, the registration at :1370), and src/config/shared/monitor/Parser.cpp (parseMode :112-145, parsePosition :147-193, parseScale :195-213)
_note: Two halves on purpose. The read half is what the page can show without asking anybody to type a resolution; the write half is the closed field list, so a key this release does not have is refused here rather than becoming a line in ~/.config/hypr/monitors.lua that the compositor answers with `hl.monitor: unknown field`. The payload this record governs is .config/hypr/monitors.lua, which hyprland.lua requires at :13 and clears from package.loaded at :9 so a reload re-runs it.

read.note: `monitors` lists the enabled outputs; `monitors all` lists the disabled ones too, because monitorsRequest walks State::monitorState()->allMonitors() instead of monitors() when the second argument is the literal `all` (src/ipc/s1/Commands.cpp:385-386). A page that offers to switch a disabled monitor back on has to ask for `all`, or the monitor it would enable is not in the list it is showing.
read.text_note: The non-JSON form starts each entry with `Monitor <name> (ID <id>):` (src/ipc/s1/Commands.cpp:326). This project always asks for -j: the text form's wording is a formatting decision upstream can change at any time, while the JSON keys are the same std::format string the code path is built from.

fields.name: name
fields.note: The output name, for example DP-1 or eDP-1. This is what `output` on the write side means.

fields.name: description
fields.note: A short human description; the value is m_shortDescription, not a sentence this project composes.

fields.name: width
fields.note: The pixel size of the mode in use, not the panel's native one.

fields.name: physicalWidth
fields.note: Millimetres, from EDID. Zero on an output that reports none, so a page dividing by it to work out a DPI has to handle zero.

fields.name: refreshRate
fields.note: Printed with five decimals, already in Hz rather than millihertz.

fields.name: activeWorkspace
fields.note: address, an optional id, type and name. The id key is only printed when the workspace has a numbered id, so a reader must not require it.

fields.name: specialWorkspace
fields.note: The same shape as activeWorkspace.

fields.name: reserved
fields.note: Four integers: left, top, right, bottom of the area layer surfaces have taken. This is what the bar and the dock are already costing the monitor, and it is why this project writes no `reserved` field of its own.

fields.name: scale
fields.note: A number when read and a string when written. The asymmetry is upstream's: m_scale is a float in the reply, while MONITOR_FIELDS builds `scale` with CLuaConfigString.

fields.name: focused
fields.note: True for the monitor that has focus. The page marks it, and says so before offering to disable it.

fields.name: vrr
fields.note: Whether adaptive sync is on right now, read out of the output's state -- not the -1..3 the write side takes.

fields.name: solitary
fields.note: A hexadecimal client pointer, or 0 when no client has the output to itself.

fields.name: solitaryBlockedBy
fields.note: One of the eighteen reason names in SOLITARY_REASONS_JSON.

fields.name: disabled
fields.note: Printed as the negation of m_enabled, so `disabled: true` means a rule has switched the output off.

fields.name: currentFormat
fields.note: The DRM format name in use, or an empty string when the output has none.

fields.name: mirrorOf
fields.note: The id of the monitor this one mirrors, as a string, or the literal `none`.

fields.name: availableModes
fields.note: Strings of the exact form `WxH@RR.RRHz`, built from the output's own mode list. This is the only source of resolution strings this project writes back: a mode the compositor listed is a mode the compositor accepts, and one typed into a text field is a guess.

fields.name: hardwareCursorsInUse
fields.note: Printed as the negation of shouldUseSoftwareCursors().

fields.name: hardwareDetails
fields.note: backend, hdr, chroma, bt2020 and vrrCapable, the last four read out of parsed EDID metadata.

write.note: A config-manager function, registered with Internal::setMgrFn (src/config/lua/bindings/LuaBindingsConfigRules.cpp:1370), so it exists only while the configuration is being parsed -- which is exactly when a required module such as monitors.lua runs. This project never calls it from a dispatcher or a timer. The argument must be a table (:1080-1083) and `output` must be a string (:1088-1092); either refusal is a config error, not a silent no-op.
write.unknown_field: A key that is not in MONITOR_FIELDS is refused with `hl.monitor: unknown field '<key>'` (src/config/lua/bindings/LuaBindingsConfigRules.cpp:1118-1122). That message is what makes the apply pipeline's verification step meaningful: after a reload, `hyprctl configerrors` is empty or the write was wrong, and the pipeline rolls back.
write.merges: An existing rule for the same output is copied into the parser before the table is walked (:1098-1100), so a second hl.monitor call for one output changes only the fields it names.

fields.name: output
fields.note: The output name from the read side. The rule parser also accepts `auto` and a description-based selector; the page always writes a real name it read back.

fields.name: mode
accepted: preferred (the empty string, or any value starting with `pref`)
fields.refused: A value with no `x` in it and no recognised prefix is refused with `invalid resolution` and the rule keeps the preferred mode (src/config/shared/monitor/Parser.cpp:126-141).

fields.name: position
fields.refused: An `auto-*` spelling that is not one of the eight is refused with `invalid auto direction` (src/config/shared/monitor/Parser.cpp:167-174), and an offset with no `x` is refused with `invalid offset` (:176-179).

fields.name: scale
accepted: auto (the empty string, or any value starting with `auto`)
a number as a string, at least 0.25
fields.refused: A non-numeric value is refused with `invalid scale` (src/config/shared/monitor/Parser.cpp:199-201); a number below 0.25 is refused and reset to 1 (:205-208). The type is a string, so a generator emitting `scale = 1` unquoted is a parse error rather than a scale of one.

fields.name: transform
fields.note: The wl_output_transform enumeration: 0 is normal, then the three rotations and the four flipped forms.

fields.name: disabled
fields.note: Switches the output off. Written, but only while at least one other output stays enabled: see refused_by_this_project.

fields.name: reserved_area
fields.note: A second spelling of the same field; both call p.setReserved.

fields.name: bitdepth
fields.note: Enables 10-bit only when the value is exactly 10.

fields.name: vrr
fields.note: A negative value leaves the rule's own optional unset rather than forcing VRR off.

fields.name: icc
fields.note: A path to an ICC profile.

refused_by_this_project.field: disabled on the last enabled output
refused_by_this_project.why: A monitor that is switched off cannot show the dialog that offers to switch it back on. The Display page refuses to disable an output when it is the only enabled one, and says why in the row rather than in a toast nobody can see.

The reserved area is what the shell's bar, dock and notifications are already costing each monitor, and the read side reports it. Writing a value here would fight the shell for the same edge of the screen, and the loser would be whichever surface drew last.

Mirroring collapses two outputs into one image. Combined with a scale change it is the quickest way to leave a session with no usable display, and a 15-second revert dialog is no use on a monitor that is showing somebody else's pixels.

refused_by_this_project.field: bitdepth, cm, sdr_eotf, sdrbrightness, sdrsaturation, sdr_min_luminance, sdr_max_luminance, min_luminance, max_luminance, max_avg_luminance, icc, supports_wide_color, supports_hdr, vrr
refused_by_this_project.why: Colour management, HDR and luminance. Every one of these can make a display unreadable -- a wrong ICC profile, or a min_luminance above the panel's own range, gives a black or a washed-out screen -- and unlike a scale or a resolution the result is not something a revert dialog can be read on. This project will not offer a switch it cannot guarantee to undo. The read side still reports all of them, so the Display page can show what the compositor decided.

payload.required_by: .config/hypr/hyprland.lua:13, and cleared from package.loaded at :9 so a reload re-runs it
payload.note: The shipped file is the identity rule: output "", mode "preferred", position "auto", scale "1". An empty output name matches every output, which is why a fresh install works on hardware nobody has seen. The generator this record governs writes one hl.monitor call per monitor the user configured and keeps the identity rule when there is nothing to write, so a machine with no saved monitor state behaves exactly as it does today.

safety.note: A scale or a resolution change is the one setting in this application that can leave a display unusable, so the page asks `Keep these changes?` with a countdown and restores the previous payload when no answer comes. The countdown is a dialog drawn over a session that is already running the new mode, which is why the change is applied and then confirmed rather than confirmed and then applied: a confirmation the user cannot read is not a confirmation.
safety.verify: After the reload, `hyprctl configerrors` must be empty and the monitor must still appear in `hyprctl -j monitors`. Either check failing rolls the payload back from the backup the pipeline took before writing it.
